The target above is scope guidance and takes precedence over your angle's default breadth: narrow which files or aspects you review to match it, and do not surface findings it asks to skip. Run the diff command above and review through EACH of the following cleanup lenses:

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.


### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.


### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.


### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Cover whichever lenses apply — you do not need findings from every lens; prioritize the highest-cost issues across all of them. Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — do not silently drop half-believed candidates; an independent verifier judges them next. If nothing qualifies, return an empty list.

397	+def parse_cds_fasta(path: Optional[Path]) -> Dict[str, List[Tuple[str, str]]]:
398	+    """Index cds.fna by NUCLEOTIDE accession -- not protein accession.
399	+
400	+    Unlike protein.faa (keyed by protein accessionVersion), cds.fna's defline carries the
401	+    parent nucleotide accession plus a coordinate suffix (e.g. 'PX492530.1:1-430'),
402	+    because a CDS is a coordinate range on its parent nucleotide record. A single
403	+    nucleotide accession can carry more than one CDS -- 134 in this package, mostly
404	+    ambisense S segments encoding both N and NSs on overlapping reading frames, plus a
405	+    few M segments annotated with separate G1/G2 CDS alongside a combined precursor
406	+    entry. parse_fasta's setdefault-first-wins index would silently keep whichever CDS
407	+    happened to be read first and drop the other, so this keeps every distinct
408	+    (product, sequence) pair per accession and leaves selection to select_primary_cds.
409	+    """
410	+    index: DefaultDict[str, List[Tuple[str, str]]] = defaultdict(list)
411	+    seen: set = set()
412	+    for desc, seq in _iter_fasta_records(path):
413	+        if not desc:
414	+            continue
415	+        tokens = desc.split(None, 1)
416	+        acc = tokens[0].split(":")[0]
417	+        base = accession_base(acc)
418	+        product = tokens[1].split("[")[0].strip() if len(tokens) > 1 else ""
419	+        seq = seq.upper()

423	+        if dedupe_key in seen:
424	+            continue
425	+        seen.add(dedupe_key)

588	+def _patristic_distance_matrix(tree: Any, labels: Sequence[str]) -> Any:

590	+    clades = {clade.name: clade for clade in tree.get_terminals()}

The exception propagates out of _analyze_species, out of run_phylogenetics_stage, and out of run_pipeline uncaught, crashing the whole program with a traceback. Because this block (all_hanta.py lines ~3290-3298) runs before `logging.info("Writing outputs")` and all the safe_write_parquet calls for ortho_accession_table, ortho_species_table, ortho_isolate_table, ortho_risk_table, the ML tables, etc., a single species hitting this gap means a --phylogenetics run produces ZERO output files at all -- not just a missing/failed reassortment row for that species -- directly contradicting the code's own docstring ('a species/segment failure never aborts the run... the same per-unit error isolation transform_one_record uses') and the README's 'nothing is silently dropped' / byte-for-byte-unaffected-default claims, since the only way to get any output on a --phylogenetics run is for every single one of potentially dozens of species-level tree builds to hit no post-tree-build exception at all.

candidates.failure_scenario: A user filtering ortho_reassortment_table.parquet on n_taxa_in_species_tree to see how close an excluded species was to the --phylo-min-taxa threshold (e.g. to decide whether to lower it and re-run) sees 0 for every below-threshold species regardless of whether it had 1 candidate or phylo_min_taxa-1 candidates, silently discarding information that group_candidates_by_species already computed (it logs 'only {len(members)} candidate(s), need {min_taxa}' but that count never reaches the per-isolate output row).
